name: interpolate the prompt straight into the command (the Phase 2 --summary RCE, Phase 3 form)
use the naive sh_quote that backslash-escapes the quote
escape the double quote before the backslash in as_quote
drop the [ -r ] prompt-file guard, so a missing file starts an empty session
old:
guard = (
        f"[ -r {file_q} ] || "
        "{ echo 'bridge: prompt file missing' >&2; exit 1; }"
    )
    return f"{guard}; cd {sh_quote(spec.project_path)} && {' '.join(argv)}"

name: drop the double quotes around $(cat ...), so word splitting shatters the prompt
join the background argv into one shell string
old:
argv.append(spec.prompt)  # exactly one element, verbatim
    return argv
new:
argv.append(spec.prompt)  # exactly one element, verbatim
    return [" ".join(argv)]

name: restore --session-id to the background argv on the spec's authority
skip the title sanitiser, so control bytes reach the terminal title
old:
kept = "".join(c for c in first if c.isprintable())
    return kept.strip()[:limit]

name: always emit --model and --effort, so an empty --model '' appears
new:
argv += ["--model", sh_quote(spec.model or "")]
    argv += ["--effort", sh_quote(spec.effort or "")]

name: hardcode claude's path the way gitprobe hardcodes git
validate the prompt after resolving and quoting instead of before
old:
validate_prompt(spec.prompt)
    claude = claude or resolve_claude()
    file_q = sh_quote(str(prompt_path))
new:
claude = claude or resolve_claude()
    file_q = sh_quote(str(prompt_path))
    validate_prompt(spec.prompt)

name: accept an unvalidated session id on the unquoted command line
old:
if not SESSION_ID_RE.match(spec.session_id):
            raise LaunchError(f"session id {spec.session_id!r} is not lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 hex")
